facts.fact: Coore & Crenshaw, opened 2020, on the headland at the north end of the resort.
Tom Doak's earlier layout (2000) had 13 greens, A to M, with no set holes; six sat on promontories above Whiskey Run Beach. Retired fire engines watered them.
The club's own logo is a shepherd's crook between the letters S and R (avoided here).

current.subject: A black-faced sheep standing on a clifftop.
current.keep: The sheep, and the black face against white wool.
current.weaknesses: The whole animal plus a cliff block is too much for 32 px; the sheep's head is tiny.

concepts.name: Black-Face
concepts.rationale: The sheep's head, front on, framed by a ring of fleece: black face, ears straight out, amber eyes. The fleece becomes the badge.
concepts.symbolism: The name made literal and friendly: the ranch's one resident, looking back at you.
concepts.typography: Rokkitt Bold, a sturdy slab with a ranch-sign feel.
concepts.strengths: A perfect round silhouette; the black-on-white contrast reads at any size.

concepts.name: The Promontory
concepts.rationale: A green on the edge of a headland, flag up, the sea breaking below. Sheep Ranch has always been about greens on the cliff edge.
references: Doak's promontory greens above Whiskey Run Beach (fact)
concepts.symbolism: Golf at the edge of the continent: nothing between the pin and the Pacific.
concepts.typography: Libre Baskerville capitals, wide-tracked: calm and classic.
concepts.strengths: Tells the course's real story; reads as golf instantly.
concepts.tradeoffs: A scene in a roundel is less iconic than a single object; uses a flag.

recommendation: Concept 1. The fleece medallion is the strongest pure icon in the Bandon set. The Promontory is the better description of the golf.
